programs.name: Homestead Exemption

exemptionValue.quote: For veterans with a disability who qualify, 50 percent of the first $200,000 of actual value of the veteran's primary residence is exempted.

ptRequired.quote: rated by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs as a one hundred percent permanent disability through disability retirement benefits or has been granted individual unemployability status

TDIU alternative.current: OR those with VA Individual Unemployability (Amendment G)
TDIU alternative.quote: a veteran who has individual unemployability status shall be treated equivalently to a veteran who has a service-connected disability that has been rated as one hundred percent permanent disability

Amendment G first year.quote: would be eligible for the exemption under this amendment in property tax year 2025

survivingSpouse.quote: If a qualifying veteran has an exemption and passes away, his or her surviving spouse may apply to keep the same exemption.

programs.effectiveChanges: No change to the amount for TY2026 or TY2027. HB25-1111 (would have reset the base to 50% of the state median home value) was postponed indefinitely by House Finance on 2/24/2025. Initiative 2025-2026 #49 (full exemption for 100% P&T/TDIU veterans from property tax year 2027) had titles set 4/16/2025 but is NOT among the statewide measures certified for the November 3, 2026 ballot (Amendments 81-87, Propositions NN and 132-137). No 2025 or 2026 enacted bill changing C.R.S. 39-3-203 for veterans was found on leg.colorado.gov; the 'SB 25-xxx' lead did not resolve to any chaptered law.
programs.note: survivingSpouse should be true: the surviving spouse of a veteran who was receiving the exemption may continue it (separate Surviving Spouse application; occupancy required), and Gold Star spouses have their own parallel exemption. Also note the exemption does not transfer on a move and has no income or age test. Deadline wording in `details` ('Jan 1 - Jul 1') is right; DPT allows good-cause late filing to August 1.

programs.name: Reserve Component Deferral

type.correct: deferral (loan), not an exemption; exclude from dollar totals
type.quote: Not verified this pass: treasury.colorado.gov/property-tax-deferral-program returned HTTP 403 to automated checks.

programs.note: This is the state Treasurer's active-military deferral under C.R.S. 39-3.5 (taxes are postponed and repaid with interest at sale or transfer), available to Guard/Reserve members called to federal active duty, not to rated veterans. It should not be credited as a dollar benefit to a rated veteran's home. Program text could not be re-read on the Treasurer's site (403); leaving the row's description unverified rather than restating it.

summary: Colorado's 50%-of-first-$200,000 exemption for 100% permanent or TDIU veterans is confirmed and unchanged for TY2026 and TY2027; survivingSpouse should flip to true, and the Reserve Component row is a deferral that should not count as a dollar benefit for a rated veteran. The full-exemption Initiative #49 did not reach the November 2026 ballot and HB25-1111 died in committee, so no pending change was found.
